svg.title: Normal-planning count rises as target effect shrinks
svg.desc: Variance-only normal-approximation reading aid for an equal-weighted three-family panel. Curves first derive a diagnostic retained count using the conservative first Holm threshold alpha/4 and 90% target, then choose the smallest planned count whose exact binomial lower tail gives 95% experiment-level retention assurance under 10% pre-response attrition. The dashed cyan curve is the baseline-variance calculation without attrition. Variances and effect sizes are illustrative dimensionless inputs, not pilot estimates, biological constants, observed model performance, calibrated bootstrap power, a frozen sample size, or comparison evidence. The final analyzer can have a higher data-dependent p-value floor when bootstrap resamples have zero standard error, so pilot-transcript simulation remains mandatory. Runtime failures remain in the denominator; support coverage is a separate gate.
svg.text: Normal-planning count rises as target effect shrinks
n_eff proportional to sigma^2/delta^2; choose n_plan by a binomial retention bound
support floor is a gate, not an n multiplier
minimum relevant candidate improvement δ (lower loss is better)
planned independent system instances per family · log scale
Variance-only normal diagnostic · Holm α/4=0.0125 · target=0.90 · bootstrap calibration open
